extracted.intended_audience: scientists, research-integrity professionals, and readers interested in research misconduct and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or evaluating news coverage about scientific article retractions and the integrity investigations that motivate them; focuses on communicating reasons for retraction, institutional responses, and community reaction. Useful for journalists, research-integrity communicators, and interested scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article must be supported by its data
rubrics_metrics.description: "Physical Review Letters concurs that the article is not supported by its data and that it needs to be retracted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after investigation, the journal determines the published claims are not supported by the underlying data, retraction is appropriate. Notices may state that the article is not supported by its data as the core reason for retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data must be locatable and available
rubrics_metrics.description: "After repeated attempts to locate the raw data and obtain an authoritative account of its origins..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and investigators should be able to request and obtain raw data. Failure to produce or locate raw data when its provenance is questioned supports concern about the integrity of reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data provenance / origins must be clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns were raised "regarding the origins and integrity of the transport data" and several figures/tables were "provided solely by Ranga P. Dias."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must be able to document where data came from and who collected/processed it. When specific figures or tables have unclear origins, journals and institutions investigate those elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals may issue an Expression of Concern during investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal published an "expression of concern" stating it was investigating concerns "regarding the origins and integrity..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Expression of Concern is an interim public notice that flags potential problems while investigation continues. News reporting should explain that such notices precede possible retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction can proceed without all authors' agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ranga P. Dias stands by the data in the aforementioned figures and table, and does not agree to retract the paper. The remaining authors regret any confusion..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retractions may be issued by journals when evidence warrants it even if one or more authors do not consent; reporting should note when authors disagree with the retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coauthors' responsibility to raise concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: "A majority of the co-authors of this study raised concerns about the origins of the superconductivity in this study as presented in Fig. 1C, Fig. 2, Fig. 3..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coauthors who identify problematic data or analyses should raise concerns with the journal or institution; such collective action can trigger Expressions of Concern and retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions should investigate allegations of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The University of Rochester "is investigating his work" and Washington State University "is also investigating allegations of plagiarism in his thesis."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When journals or peers flag problems, authors' institutions have responsibility to investigate possible misconduct (e.g., data fabrication, plagiarism) and report findings; coverage should note institutional investigations and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should identify specific problematic figures/tables and summarize steps taken
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice lists specific figures and table sections in question and states attempts were made to locate raw data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear retraction notices name the affected elements (figures/tables/sections) and summarize investigative steps (e.g., requests for raw data), improving transparency for readers and downstream researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: High citation counts do not guarantee validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The article has been cited 178 times, according to information presented on its abstract page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters and evaluators should recognize that widely cited papers can still be retracted; citation metrics are not a substitute for data integrity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and data-processing procedures must be transparent and not misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigation impacted the "presented data and method for removing background" and noted a probable explanation that measured data were computed by adding UDB_1R to the published data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must fully disclose data-processing steps (e.g., background subtraction) and not present misleading procedures; opaque or deceptive methods are grounds for scrutiny and potential retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary claims require independent replication and scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters note that claims like room-temperature superconductivity invite intense scrutiny and that many results are non-reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When published claims are extraordinary, independent replication by multiple labs and transparent sharing of methods/data are essential; lack of reproducibility increases suspicion of error or misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community expectations about consequences for proven misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments propose strong consequences (e.g., stripping degree, firing) and criticize systemic incentives like "publish or perish."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While consequences vary by institution and finding, community sentiment often expects substantive penalties for deliberate fabrication or plagiarism; reporting should distinguish allegation, investigation, and proven misconduct before describing sanctions.
